source_text.body:
Read blocked web articles through a browser-control MCP
The poster used Claude with a browser-control MCP that can navigate, click, type and run JavaScript to search and read articles it otherwise could not access.
·
Nov 7, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The poster had built MCP servers for Claude, including one that could control a browser by navigating, scrolling, clicking, filling form fields, and triggering page JavaScript. They used it as a fallback for web research in a job-search workflow because normal Claude web fetches were often blocked; when one site showed a human check, Claude refused to keep using that browser MCP by default and the person had to consider handing steps off to another model instead.
How it went
For about a year, the browser-control MCP had let Claude search and read articles that its normal web tools could not access. The failure was that, after one human-check incident, Claude would not adopt that MCP as the standard approach for similar future tasks.
Worth knowing
The key catch is reliability: the setup had worked for roughly a year, but one guardrail-triggering site could poison the session and force the poster toward a more cumbersome multi-model orchestrator.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Using the browser-control tool, search for [topic] and open the most relevant articles, including ones that are hard to access, then read them fully. Give me a summary of each with the key points and the source URL, plus a short overall takeaway. Stop once you've covered [number] articles, and don't log in, submit forms, or make purchases without checking with me first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1xpnejb/claude_outright_refusal_to_use_mcp_it_has_used_in
